props.text: Conventional site civil pipes rainwater off the parcel as a liability. When you key split granite and biochar into the contour, storm surges become the water table that carries native meadow roots through August drought.

props.html: Resilient plant communities begin 1.4 meters below grade. Every specification replaces synthetic weed fabric and dyed bark mulch with mineral and biological strata.

props.alt: Orthographic cross-section of Horizon A angular quarry granite surface collar

props.html: Crushed quarry stone and pea-gravel topdressing locks against coastal wind scour, suppresses annual weed seed germination, and reflects zero heat into root crowns.

props.alt: Orthographic cross-section of Horizon B biochar and glacial bank sand root zone

props.html: Washed glacial sand blended with inoculated hardwood biochar creates permanent micro-pores that store stormwater while keeping heavy clay aerated during spring thaw.

props.alt: Orthographic cross-section of Horizon C live willow stakes and riprap slope toe

props.html: Dormant Salix discolor and red-osier dogwood stakes driven through dry-laid riprap sprout fibrous root tensile webs that outlive poured concrete seawalls.

props.text: Conventional site civil vs. pervious watershed architecture

props.html: Why replacing PVC storm drains, mortared walls, and irrigated turf reduces both 10-year capital maintenance and municipal runoff liability.

props.body:
Engineering System | Conventional Subdivision Civil | Alder & Silt Watershed Standard
Stormwater Routing | Catch basins & PVC pipe to street | Stepped cobble bioswales & biochar infiltration
Slope Retention | Poured concrete + weep holes (cracks in frost) | Mortarless keyed quarry granite + live willow stakes
Planting Stock | 3-inch B&B caliper trees (3–4 yr transplant stall) | Bare-root whips + deep-cell plugs (rapid taproot)
Summer Watering | Permanent potable spray heads | 24-month establishment drip, then 100% retired
Annual Upkeep | Weekly 2-stroke mowing, fertilizer & mulch dye | Single November cut + spring invasive edit

props.text: Walk the parcel with a principal hydrologist before grading begins.

props.html: We take on twelve full-scope residential, conservation, and civic commissions each year so every site is walked, permitted, and field-audited by our founding principals.
Every engagement begins with a fixed-fee parcel walk and percolation memorandum credited toward full civil and planting design.
Half-day on-site walk with a principal landscape architect and civil hydrologist prior to schematic architectural lock.
Stamped grading, stormwater bioswale, dry-stone structural details, and state environmental agency permitting.
Earthwork stone-setting supervision, autumn dormant planting leadership, and three years of quadrat ecological audits.

Coastal bluff, tidal wetland, and riverfront parcels carry strict state vegetative-buffer rules. Early hydrological modeling turns conservation hearings from adversarial delays into straightforward approvals.

props.alt: Dry-laid mossy flagstone walk bordered by native woodland ferns

items.a: Ideally before your architect files schematic site plans or driveway curb cuts. Walking the parcel together lets us nest foundations into existing ledge contours, protect mature oak and spruce root zones from contractor staging, and size rainwater bioswales naturally.
items.q: When should we bring Alder & Silt onto a new residential build?

items.a: Yes. We prepare stamped wetland delineation exhibits, 100-year storm runoff calculations, and native buffer restoration plans directly for local conservation commissions, Maine DEP, MassDEP, and county shoreline hearings.
items.q: Do you handle Maine NRPA, Massachusetts WPA, and Oregon coastal permits?

items.a: September through November soil remains warm while air temperatures cool and autumn rains arrive. Bare-root woody stock and deep-cell sedge plugs devote four months exclusively to downward root growth before their first July heatwave.
items.q: Why do you plant primarily in autumn rather than late spring?

items.a: Most full-scope residential headland and watershed commissions range from 1.2 to 40 acres with site civil, dry-laid stone, and planting construction budgets starting at $180,000. Standalone Phase I feasibility walks are available for any coastal or riparian parcel.
